issues.legal_issue: The qualifying assessment-year language in the wealth-tax exemption proviso limits the gifts eligible for exemption by reference to the gift-tax assessment year.
material_facts: The assets had been transferred to a spouse or minor child and would otherwise have been included in the transferor’s wealth.
The gifts in the appeals were made before the relevant qualifying period, although they were chargeable to gift tax.
The assessees claimed that the exemption applied to the assets in later wealth-tax assessments regardless of when the gifts were made.
issues.conclusion: The qualifying assessment-year language refers to gift-tax assessments, not wealth-tax assessments. Gifts outside the qualifying period do not receive the exemption and remain includible in the transferor’s net wealth. The Revenue’s appeal was allowed and the assessees’ appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The plain language of section 4(1)(a) of the Wealth-tax Act, 1957, and its proviso controls: the phrase concerning an assessment year commencing after the specified date qualifies the gift-tax assessment. The proviso applies where a transfer is chargeable to gift tax or is not chargeable under section 5 of the Gift-tax Act, 1958, but only where the gift meets the qualifying-period condition. The Court approved the construction adopted in T. Saraswathi Achi v. C.I.T., 104 ITR 195; C.W.T. v. Seth Nand Lal Ganeriwala, 107 ITR 758; M.G. Kollankulam v. C.I.T., 115 ITR 160; Malti Harseey v. C.W.T., 12 ITR 676; and C.W.T. v. Rasesh N. Mafatlal, 126 ITR 173.

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment_proceeding: A proceeding assesses the transferor’s wealth and determines whether transferred assets are included.
predicates.asset_would_otherwise_be_included_in_tra: The transferred asset would be included in the transferor’s wealth apart from the claimed exemption.
predicates.gift_tax_assessment_outside_eligible_per: The gift-tax assessment for the transfer falls outside the period that qualifies the gift for the exemption.

issues.definition: When a wealth-tax assessment concerns an asset otherwise includible in the transferor’s wealth and the gift-tax assessment falls outside the eligible period, the asset remains includible.

issues.legal_issue: A construction chosen to avoid unconstitutionality cannot replace the plain meaning of statutory language that admits only one reasonable interpretation.
material_facts: The assessees proposed a different reading of the proviso to avoid an asserted discriminatory effect.

The Court concluded that the proviso’s language could be read only as referring to gift-tax assessments, and that the proposed alternative conflicted with the provision’s wording and legislative operation.
issues.conclusion: The Court applied the plain meaning and rejected the alternative construction; the rule preferring a constitutional construction is available only when the statutory language reasonably permits more than one interpretation.
issues.legal_principle: The literal rule requires courts to apply clear statutory language regardless of the result. Constitutional avoidance may guide a choice only between two reasonably possible readings; it cannot alter clear words. The Court relied on State of Punjab v. Prem Sukhdas, [1977] 3 SCR 408, and referred to Attorney General v. Carlton Bank, [1899] 2 Q.B. 158, in explaining the ordinary duty to give effect to legislative language.

predicates.statutory_interpretation_proceeding: A court is asked to determine the meaning of statutory language.
predicates.statutory_text_has_only_one_reasonable_m: The statutory language, properly construed, permits only one reasonable interpretation.
predicates.alternative_reading_is_proposed_to_avoid: A party proposes a different interpretation to avoid an asserted constitutional defect.

issues.definition: If a statutory interpretation proceeding involves clear language with only one reasonable meaning, a proposed alternative to avoid invalidity does not displace the plain text.

issues.legal_issue: A court deciding a statutory reference does not examine or pronounce upon the constitutionality of the statute.
material_facts: The matter came before the Court as a reference arising under a statute.
The assessees argued that the Revenue’s interpretation would expose the provision to a constitutional challenge based on discrimination.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not decide the provision’s constitutionality, stating that this was a matter for judicial review rather than determination in the statutory reference.
issues.legal_principle: In a reference arising under a statute, the court does not examine and pronounce upon the statute’s constitutionality. State of Punjab v. Prem Sukhdas, [1977] 3 SCR 408, supports the limit on using interpretation to alter clear statutory language; the Court distinguished constitutional review as a separate judicial function.

predicates.statutory_reference_proceeding: A matter is before the court as a reference arising under a statute.
predicates.constitutional_validity_is_put_in_issue: A party raises a claim that the statute is constitutionally invalid.

issues.definition: When constitutional validity is raised in a statutory reference proceeding, the court does not determine that validity.
